title: GOST Collision Attack Without Repeated-Half Chaining Values
summary: The strategy relies on a repeated-half chaining value, and a related attack checks two to the thirty-second power values; finding a collision below that cost without the structure remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the GOST hash function, determine whether the attack strategy that finds a collision by exploiting an initial chaining value of the form $H_{i-1}=(x,x)$ can find a collision with fewer than $2^{32}$ hash-function evaluations when the initial chaining value $H_{i-1}$ does not have that form. The existing strategy relies on $H_{i-1}=(x,x)$, and the related attack checks $2^{32}$ chaining values until it obtains one with this form before applying the attack.

scope.domain: Collision cryptanalysis of the GOST hash function, focusing on the structure of chaining values.
assumptions: The existing attack strategy relies on an initial chaining value of the form $H_{i-1}=(x,x)$.
parameters: $H_{i-1}$: the initial chaining value and whether it has the repeated-half form $(x,x)$
$2^{32}$: the existing chaining-value search count and the hash-function evaluation threshold to beat
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the strategy can find a collision with fewer than $2^{32}$ hash-function evaluations when the initial chaining value is not of the form $(x,x)$.

citations.label: Practical-Time Related-Key Attack on GOST with Secret S-boxes

progress.summary: The source identifies the existing strategy's dependence on $H_{i-1}=(x,x)$ and reports that the related attack checks $2^{32}$ chaining values before applying it. It leaves open whether the strategy can achieve a collision with fewer than $2^{32}$ hash-function evaluations from other initial values.
citation_labels: Ariel Weizman et al., Practical-Time Related-Key Attack on GOST with Secret S-boxes
